body.statement:
For every \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_L)\in\{-1/2,1/2\}^L\), the fixed block-homogeneous schedule \(m_v\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}hard	ext{-}subexperiment	ext{-}embedding}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_n(B)\), because it is fixed and all outcomes lie in \([-1/2,1/2]\); moreover, \(\mu_l^v(a)=v_l\), \(\mu_l^v(b)=0\), and \(	heta(m_v)=\sum_{l=1}^Lw_lv_l=T(v)\). Under \(m_v\), \(K_l=A_l=\mathbf 1\{Z_{B_l}=\mathbf 1_{B_l}\}\), the \(K_l\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_l)\), \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=K_lv_l\) for \(i\in B_l\), and \(O_l=(K_l,K_lv_l)\) is measurable from \(D\). The remaining assignment information is retained exactly: \(\operatorname{Law}(Z\mid K=k)= igotimes_{l=1}^L
u_{l,k_l}\), where \(
u_{l,1}=\delta_{\mathbf 1_{B_l}}\) and \(
u_{l,0}=\operatorname{Uniform}(\{0,1\}^{B_l}\setminus\{\mathbf 1_{B_l}\})\), so the \(K_l=0\) branch includes all-control and every mixed pattern with their original conditional probabilities. With the measure-preserving splitter \( eta(R)=(R_0,R_1,\ldots,R_L)\), the samplers \(F_l\), and \(D^*\) of the same definition, \(\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)=\Gamma(D^*(O,R_1,\ldots,R_L),R_0)\) is measurable in \((O,R)\) for every measurable externally randomized \(\Gamma\). For every fixed \(v\), \[\operatorname{Law}(D^*,R_0\mid V=v)=\operatorname{Law}_{Z,R_0,m_v}(D,R_0),\] and therefore \[P_{K,R}\{T(v)\in\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\mid V=v\}=P_{Z,R_0,m_v}\{	heta(m_v)\in\Gamma(D,R_0)\},\qquad \mathbb E_{K,R}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\mid V=v]=\mathbb E_{Z,R_0,m_v}[\operatorname{len}\{\Gamma(D,R_0)\}].\] Consequently, if \(\Gamma\in\mathfrak C_\alpha\), then \(\Lambda_\Gamma\) has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) for every fixed \(v\), \(Q_t\{T(V)\in\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{tilt}}\), and \[\sup_{m'\in\mathcal M_n(B)}\mathbb E_{Z,R,m'}[\operatorname{len}\{\Gamma(D,R)\}]\ge\sup_{v\in\{-1/2,1/2\}^L}\mathbb E_{K,R}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\mid V=v]\ge\mathbb E_{Q_t}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}]\] for every admissible \(t\). Taking the supremum over admissible \(t\), applying a weighted-erasure spread result if and when it is proved, and then taking the infimum over \(\Gamma\in\mathfrak C_\alpha\) yields the minimax lower bound. Thus the bridge preserves the entire randomized decision experiment; it does not assert the weighted-erasure posterior-spread inequality.
body.justification: This exact Markov-kernel embedding retains every assignment ancillary and transfers pointwise coverage and expected length for arbitrary externally randomized original-data intervals.
body.gap: The weighted-erasure lower experiment is not automatically a subexperiment for arbitrary procedures unless the unrevealed assignment patterns and external randomization are reconstructed with their exact laws.
body.consumer: The posterior-spread question and no-dominance minimax theorem can invoke a rigorous experiment-to-experiment reduction without assuming ancillary irrelevance.
